steps.determines: UNIQUE (fixed by the flat triangular growth)
steps.expr: flat triangular lattice puts 6r registrations on ring r; |B_r| = 1 + sum_{k<=r} 6k = 1 + 3r(r+1)
steps.what: the flat reference flat_ball(r) = 1 + 3r(r+1): the defect-zero ball count
steps.why: the deficit needs a reference: what |B_r| WOULD be with zero defect. In the flat triangular lattice (every vertex degree 6) ring r carries exactly 6r registrations, so flat_ball(r) = 1 + sum_{k=1..r} 6k = 1 + 3r(r+1). It is a COUNT, not an area -- 'flat' here means defect zero, not an embedded plane. This is the yardstick B.2 measures the substrate against.

steps.check: D = flat - |B_r|; deg-5 profile (0,1,3,6,10); all D >= 0 on R4 (spherical side)
steps.determines: SIGNED; here D >= 0 (the spherical side); 0 is the flat mirror
steps.expr: D_r(v) = flat_ball(r) - |B_r(v)|; > 0 spherical, = 0 flat (mirror), < 0 hyperbolic; here D >= 0

value.sign_convention: D>0 spherical, D=0 flat (mirror), D<0 hyperbolic

steps.what: the density deficit D_r(v) = flat_ball(r) - |B_r(v)|: SIGNED curvature
steps.why: the DENSITY DEFICIT is D_r(v) = flat_ball(r) - |B_r(v)|: how many registrations are missing from v's r-neighbourhood compared with a flat one of the same relational radius. It is SIGNED curvature -- D > 0 means the ball grows SLOWER than flat (positive/spherical curvature), D = 0 is flat (the mirror; a degree-6 site in open country), and D < 0 would be faster-than-flat (hyperbolic). This CLOSED 2-sphere realizes D >= 0 at every vertex (checked on R4), largest at the twelve degree-5 sites -- the positive side of the mirror. The chirality reading ('0 is a mirror, left-handed natural') is a downstream physical claim, not derived here.

steps.check: deg-5 deficit = r(r+1)/2 = 1,3,6,10, clean at R3/R4; R2 r=3 = 11 (finite-size), recorded
steps.determines: UNIQUE (the closed form; asserted where the ball is free)
steps.expr: for deg-5 v: D_r(v) = r(r+1)/2 (= 1,3,6,10 for r=1..4), level-independent; R2 r=3 is a finite-size exception (11, not 6)
steps.what: the primordial law: the deficit at each of the twelve is the triangular number r(r+1)/2
steps.why: at each of the twelve degree-5 registrations the deficit has an exact closed form: D_r = the r-th TRIANGULAR number r(r+1)/2 (1, 3, 6, 10, ...), INDEPENDENT of refinement level. The curvature is concentrated on the twelve and its integrated (ball-count) form is triangular -- the constant second difference of r(r+1)/2 is 1, one unit of curvature per step per carrier. ONE finite-size exception is recorded rather than smoothed: at R2, r=3 the value is 11 not 6, because a 42-vertex mesh is too small for a radius-3 ball to develop freely; the law is asserted where the ball does not compete with the far side of the bound -- clean at R3 and R4.

steps.check: angle deficit = 2 per deg-5, 0 per deg-6; total 24 = 12*chi at every level
steps.determines: UNIQUE (Gauss-Bonnet; the charge is fixed by chi)
steps.expr: angle-defect (12 - 2*deg) = 2 radits per deg-5, 0 per deg-6; sum = 24 = 12*chi at every level
steps.what: the curvature charge: the angle deficit sums to 12*chi = 24 (Gauss-Bonnet), invariant
steps.why: the CONCENTRATED curvature -- distinct from the ball deficit and named separately so they are never merged. An equilateral triangulation gives a degree-d vertex the angle defect 2pi - d*(pi/3) = (12 - 2d) radits (12 radits = 2pi). That is 2 radits at each of the twelve degree-5 vertices and 0 everywhere else, so the total is 24 = 12*chi (chi = 2) -- Gauss-Bonnet, and REFINEMENT-INVARIANT (subdivision adds only degree-6 vertices, which carry no charge). This is the Regge curvature as an exact integer charge, per-vertex and r-INDEPENDENT: a DIFFERENT object from B.2/B.3's r-resolved ball deficit, though both concentrate on the twelve.

steps.check: sum_v deficit is level-invariant per radius: r=1:12, r=2:96, r=3:372, r=4:1020
steps.determines: UNIQUE (invariant of the bound at each radius)
steps.expr: sum_v [flat_ball(r) - |B_r(v)|] is the SAME at every level: r=1:12, r=2:96, r=3:372, r=4:1020
steps.what: the ball-deficit total sum_v D_r(v) is refinement-invariant per radius (a 2nd conservation)
steps.why: summed over the whole mesh, the ball deficit at each radius is IDENTICAL at every refinement level -- exactly, including where the per-vertex distribution differs. r=1 -> 12, r=2 -> 96, r=3 -> 372, r=4 -> 1020, each invariant across the levels on which the ball fits. This is a conservation law of the same SHAPE as 12*chi, and it is what makes the deficit an observable of the BOUND rather than an artefact of how finely the bound has been divided. It is a SECOND, r-resolved conservation -- kept distinct from B.4's angle-deficit charge, which it is not equal to (12, 96, 372, 1020 are not 24).
